newsitem.title: USA: American Brands reports lower profits.
newsitem.headline: American Brands reports lower profits.

text.p: American Brands Inc., whose products range from Jim Beam whiskey to Master Lock padlocks, reported lower profits Friday, due in part to charges from restructuring and disposed businesses.

American Brands said its profits fell to $114 million, or 65 cents a share, in the fourth quarter from $154.1 million, or 83 cents a share, in the year earlier period. Sales rose to $3.43 billion, compared with $3.08 billion a year earlier.

American Brands owns distilled spirits brands including Jim Beam; hardware and home improvement brands including Moen faucets, Master locks and Aristokraft cabinets; and golf brands include Titleist and Cobra.
Its Gallaher Ltd. unit sells tobacco products internationally, principally in Europe, where its major brands include Benson and Hedges and Silk Cut.
In October, the company announced plans to spin off Gallaher to its shareholders. Steps to implement the spin-off are progressing, it said.
When the transaction is completed, possibly by mid-year, the company said it plans to change the name American Brands to Fortune Brands.
For the year, earnings were $486.5 million, or $2.74 a share, after some charges and discontinued items. A year earlier it earned $540.4 million, or $2.83 a share, in 1995.
For the year, sales rose to $11.58 billion from $11.37 billion.
Restructuring charges in 1996 related to a plant consolidation in international tobacco, the worldwide reorganization of distilled spirits operations and disposed businesses.
American Brands stock fell 62.5 cents to $52.25 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
